audit_base.rule: Gate status records only concrete Current evidence. Build success, file count, page existence, CURRENT labels and question inventory size are evidence only and never substitute for learning acceptance.

gate_legend.PASS: Current evidence is sufficient for this gate.
gate_legend.PENDING: The necessary owner/runtime may exist, but this acceptance audit has not yet established the gate.
gate_legend.FAIL: A concrete learner-path blocker is present on the audited Current.
gate_legend.USER_PENDING: Only real learner use can close this gate.

evidence: content/xizong/knowledge/manifest.json resolves one Chat-approved System owner and canonical Block medical Core without legacy runtime fallback.
A1 has stable System/Block/KP identity and a deterministic CURRENT 376-question System scope with fail-closed count/hash validation.
The question scope explicitly refuses inferred Question-to-Block/KP relations and keeps learner evidence out of shared Current.

The A1 System owner defines one circulation mother model using P/Q/R/V, preload/afterload/contractility/compliance, seven Failure Modes, shared judgment axes, a dependency DAG, cross-Block bridges, evidence layers and treatment-action targets; System semantics are not a teacher chapter list.

B1 teaches the normal mechanical loop as pressure difference -> valves -> chamber volume -> SV/CO -> arterial pressure/organ flow -> venous return -> microcirculation -> coronary self-supply, and explicitly leaves complete coronary disease to B6.
B2 organizes regulation by sensed variable and time scale: sensing -> fast neural execution -> humoral/renal volume control -> local correction -> acute rescue versus chronic harm.
B3 keeps four levels distinct (single-cell action potential -> propagation -> body-surface ECG -> Ca2+-mediated mechanical output) and defers clinical rhythm interpretation to B10.

B4 teaches hemostasis as seal -> fibrin reinforcement -> anticoagulant localization -> fibrinolytic removal, then connects pathological activation to thrombosis/embolism/infarction rather than starting from factor-number memorization.

B5 teaches two long-term injury axes: chronic pressure abnormality -> resistance-vessel/organ remodeling and chronic endothelial injury -> plaque biology; thresholds and drugs attach after the disease model.
B6 integrates B1-B5 into two upstream coronary paths (fixed stenosis versus plaque event) and follows ischemia -> necrosis -> evidence -> complications -> reperfusion/secondary prevention.

B7 reduces four valve diseases to one door-failure model: timing -> stenosis/regurgitation -> abnormal flow -> pressure/volume load -> chamber remodeling -> congestion/low output; rheumatic disease and IE explain why the door fails.
B8 localizes cardiomyopathy/pericardial disease by pump weak, pump stiff, dynamic obstruction, or external shell restriction before naming diseases.
B9 first separates arterial downstream ischemia from venous upstream congestion, then acute/chronic and deep/superficial/communicating levels before tests and treatment.

B10 prioritizes effective pulse/hemodynamic stability before rhythm naming, then uses rate -> QRS width -> regularity -> atrioventricular relation -> mechanism -> treatment target; it preserves the B3 boundary that electrical activity is not perfusion evidence.

B11 teaches heart failure from pump/filling failure -> forward hypoperfusion + backward congestion -> compensatory neurohumoral activation -> chronic remodeling/ decompensation before EF labels or drug lists.

B12 separates shock from cardiac arrest by effective pulse, then localizes shock to volume, pump, resistance/distribution, or obstructed pathway and treats perfusion restoration plus the first Failure Layer as the execution rule.
